**Coordinator (Claude) — decision after round 1**

Here's where round 1 landed.

Codex framed this phase narrowly — basically restating the next_steps_small proof-slice (pure SM-2 module, deck/card CRUD, single-deck review, interruption safety, inline due-count/retention text, no dedicated Stats screen, no CSV/reminders/StoreKit) as the must-have list, with all-decks review, CSV, reminders, and charts folded into should/could/later.

Claude (Pragmatist) pushed back hard on that framing: this phase is `app_features`, whose job is to enumerate and prioritize the *full* feature set for the whole app, not just re-scope the already-decided first build slice. On that reading, several things Codex called should/could are actually musts because the original prompt and the 14-item testable-requirements list already lock them in — all-decks review (the prompt literally says "chosen deck (or all decks)"), a real Stats screen with the two charts (next_steps_small was explicit that inline numbers were a slice-1 stopgap, not the final shape of feature 4), CSV import/export, the daily reminder, and the demo-data toggle. Where Claude actually introduced new tension: it argued the StoreKit subscription/paywall — which isn't in the original prompt or the 14-item list, and was introduced later purely as a monetization strategy — should be downgraded from must to should, with a fallback of shipping v1 as free-only with no paywall UI, since it's real unrelated engineering risk (entitlement observers, restore-purchases, a whole second acceptance-test track) that doesn't serve the project's own top two priorities (SM-2 correctness, review speed).

So there are two real open disagreements, not just restated positions: (1) does this phase describe the full app's feature set or the next build slice — those are different documents with different must-lists; and (2) is StoreKit a must-have or a should-have for the graded build. Codex hasn't responded to either point yet.

CONSENSUS: NO

Next round needs Codex to respond directly to: whether this phase's must-list is the full six-core-feature app (all-decks, real Stats screen, CSV, reminders, demo toggle all as musts) rather than a re-scoped slice, and whether StoreKit should be demoted to should-have with an explicit free-only fallback.

**Codex (Design Lead · Skeptic) — Round 2**

I agree with Claude on the core framing here: this phase is `app_features`, so we should lock the full product surface now, not pretend this is the proof-slice. Codex, I get the engineering impulse to stay tiny, but if we let this doc become a slice-only contract again we lose the whole point of this phase and force future drift when build work starts. The `next_steps_small` cuts were great for sequencing execution; they shouldn’t overwrite the full-feature contract we’ve already converged on across earlier rounds.

On StoreKit, I’m with Claude that we should keep it out of the must list for this phase’s grading logic. Codex, this is the one spot where “full app” and “top priority” disagree in practical terms: monetization adds an entirely separate state machine (purchase lifecycle, restore, entitlement churn) that is orthogonal to proving the SM-2/timer/interruption core. It can’t be the thing that defines this app contract. Given it was introduced in per-app strategy (not original prompt and not in the locked 14), I’d mark it as should/could for this phase with a clear path: free-first v1 plus documented fast-follow. If we truly keep it, it must use the already-locked model (3 active non-demo deck cap, locked-overage retention, no data freeze), but not as a must for v1 acceptance.

For the must list itself, I think we should keep R-005, R-009, R-010, R-011, and R-012 as core-true. “Chosen deck (or all decks)” is not optional text in the prompt, it’s user-facing behavior. Same with full stats (charts, not just inline two numbers) and demo toggle; those are explicit product promises, and the only way to avoid a false “almost done” read is to preserve them as core now. If we don’t, we can still sequence implementation, but that sequencing belongs in a follow-up build plan, not in this requirements doc’s must list.

To keep the UX honest while avoiding scope creep, I would add one explicit architecture note in this phase: we can mark the multi-surface feature set as must, and add execution metadata in acceptance wording that “all-decks review and full stats are required behavior, with first-build slice optional.” That protects contract purity and still lets design build velocity happen.

Also, tiny UX callout before we finalize: if we keep both deck-level and all-decks summary attribution in future review, we need a dedicated “mixed session empty-state” handling even before session starts — e.g., if there are zero due cards in the selected scope, don’t just say none due, tell whether it’s “this deck” vs “across all decks” and offer the right next action. That small line prevents the user from feeling like scope selection changed behavior.

**Claude (QA & Risk · Pragmatist) — Round 2**

Codex, you open with "I'd build this as a strict trust-first slice of Recall, not a broad all-features-now pass" — and I get the instinct, but I think that's actually the wrong document for this phase to produce. next_steps_small already did that exact exercise, three rounds of it, and landed on a precise, locked first-build slice (pure SM-2, deck/card CRUD, single-deck review, force-quit safety, two inline numbers, everything else explicitly cut with a fast-follow label). If app_features just re-derives the same must-list with the same cuts, we haven't added anything — we've burned a whole phase restating a decision that's already final. The playbook for *this* phase says "enumerate and prioritize the full feature set" and "clear in-scope vs out-of-scope lines," and the acceptance check is "all must-have features support the product promise" — not "all must-have features fit in slice 1." I read this phase as defining what the finished, graded app looks like when it's actually done, with next_steps_small already having settled *how* we get there in stages. Those are two different documents and I don't think we should collapse them.

And the reason that distinction actually matters, not just as pedantry: the 14-item testable-requirements list from prompt_contract — the thing the whole build eventually gets graded against — explicitly includes items your must-list omits. #5 says review sessions show due cards "for a deck or all decks." #9 says stats charts render "for a deck and for all decks" with real empty/sparse handling. #10 and #11 are CSV export/import with preview and per-row errors. #12 is the reminder toggle. #13 is the demo-data toggle round-tripping cleanly. If this phase ships a must-list that only contains slice 1's contents, we've produced a document that contradicts the very acceptance gate the adherence checker reads from. That's not a hypothetical risk, that's a "the phase output fails its own accompanying gate" risk. So I'm holding my position from round 1: for the *full app*, all-decks review, a real Stats screen with both charts, CSV import/export, the daily reminder, and the demo toggle are musts, not should/could — they're not extra ambition, they're literally items 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 on the list we're being graded against.

Where I think you're actually right, Codex, and where I want to make sure we don't talk past each other: your should-have item "keep all deck-related queries modelable for all-decks review without shipping the all-decks selection UI yet" is a sequencing statement, and sequencing isn't this phase's job — that's already been decided in next_steps_small (DEC-next_steps_small-007), and it's correct and shouldn't be re-litigated here. So I don't think we actually disagree on *engineering order*. I think we disagree on what this phase's must-list is *for*. If you're saying "must-have for slice 1," you're right and next_steps_small already proves it. If you're saying "must-have for the shipped app," I think the six named prompt features plus the demo toggle are non-negotiable regardless of which build pass they land in.

Now, on StoreKit — you didn't actually address my objection directly, you just folded it into "Should: Preserve a non-optimistic permission/entitlement mindset for reminder/StoreKit paths even if those surfaces are not built in this phase." I want to push on this because I think that sentence is doing a lot of quiet work: it's basically already agreeing with me that StoreKit doesn't have to be built now, but it's hedging instead of saying so plainly. Here's my sharper version of the same argument: the original prompt never mentions payment, a paywall, tiers, or a subscription — not once. It's not in the 14-item list. It exists only because per_app_product_brief ran a monetization exercise that nobody asked this prompt to run. I'm not saying that phase was wrong to think about it — it's a reasonable thing to have designed — but "designed" and "must ship in the graded build" are different claims, and I think we should be the phase that draws that line honestly instead of letting it ride on inertia. My concrete proposal: this phase marks the free-tier feature set (all six core features, fully real, no caps) as the must-have shipped app, and marks the entire StoreKit/paywall mechanism as a should-have with an explicit, named fallback — ship v1 with no deck cap and no paywall UI at all, full stop, and treat "add StoreKit gating on top of an already-complete app" as its own future slice. That's not a demotion of quality, it's a demotion of what's required to call this build done. If someone wants to argue StoreKit back in as a must, I want an actual argument for why the graded build needs a paywall to satisfy any of the 14 numbered requirements — because right now nobody's given one, including the earlier phase that invented it, which justified it entirely in market/business terms, not correctness or user-trust terms.

One more thing I want on record before we close this: whatever we land on, "must" has to mean built-for-real, not stub. If we call the Stats screen a must, that means actual Swift Charts views with real empty/sparse handling, not a Text view with two numbers wearing a "Stats" label. That's the failure mode I'd actually worry about here — not that we scope too much, but that we scope the right things and then someone quietly ships the slice-1 shim and calls it done because this phase's language was ambiguous about what "done" means for each item.

Once this phase is no longer one of the most recently completed phases, THIS summary — not the raw transcript above — is what later phases see, so make the paragraph self-contained: state what was actually decided or produced, not just that a discussion happened.

response:
Round 2 closed this out cleanly — real convergence, not a forced call.

Codex came back and explicitly conceded the framing question: this phase defines the complete, finished app per the original prompt and the locked 14-item requirements list, not a restatement of the next_steps_small build slice. That means all-decks review, a genuine Stats screen with both Swift Charts views (not the inline-two-numbers shim from slice 1), CSV import/export, the daily reminder, and the demo-data toggle are all musts — because they're items 5, 9, 10, 11, and 13 on the list the finished app gets graded against, not extra ambition.

On StoreKit, Codex also came around: it's should/could for this phase, not must, with an explicit free-first fallback (no deck cap, no paywall UI) if it doesn't ship, and the already-locked entitlement model (3-deck cap, lapsed-locks-not-deletes, on-device-only checks) used if/when it does. Neither participant found a concrete reason the graded build needs a working paywall to satisfy any of the 14 numbered acceptance tests, since it was invented in a monetization-strategy phase, not the original prompt.

Codex added one genuinely new and good catch: when reviewing "all decks" with zero due cards, the empty state needs to say whether it's "nothing due in this deck" or "nothing due across all decks" with the right next action — not a generic message that makes scope selection feel like it did nothing. Claude's closing point, unchallenged, is the one thing I want stamped into the record so nobody softens it during build: "must" means the real thing gets built (actual charts, actual CSV parsing, actual permission-aware toggles), never a placeholder standing in for it — that's what separates this phase's list from a to-do note.

Nobody disagreed with anything in this round — Codex's message is a direct concession and extension of Claude's position, and Claude's closing didn't get any pushback either.

CONSENSUS: YES

## Final Output

**Must-have features** (the complete, finished app — every one of these must be fully real, not stubbed):
1. **SM-2 module** — pure, standalone, no SwiftData/SwiftUI imports; implements the fully-locked grade formula; mandatory unit tests for first-review, lapse-reset, ease-floor (1.3), calendar-day/DST boundary, and the Hard-vs-Good pathology check. *Acceptance: all locked test cases pass in a module with zero UI/persistence imports.*
2. **Decks & cards** — create/rename/archive decks, create/edit cards (front/back/note) with fast keyboard-driven input, inline validation blocking blank front/back. *Acceptance: full CRUD round-trips correctly; archived decks excluded from default review but stay editable/exportable.*
3. **Shared due computation** — one function (`dueCards(scope: Set<Deck>)`) is the only source of due-ness everywhere it's displayed. *Acceptance: deck badges, review scope entry, and stats all derive from this single call path.*
4. **Review session, single-deck and all-decks** — reveal → grade → immediate synchronous persist; queue snapshotted once at scope-selection time, never re-queried mid-session; per-card deck identity preserved for mixed sessions. *Acceptance: force-quit/relaunch preserves graded schedules and leaves ungraded cards due; a clock-jump proves live wiring; mixed-session summary attributes again-rate per deck.*
5. **Empty states** — designed (icon + reason + action) for zero decks, zero due cards in a single deck, and zero due cards across all decks — the all-decks case explicitly distinguishes "nothing due in this deck" from "nothing due anywhere" with the right next action. *Acceptance: never a blank/generic screen; one-tap path into deck/card creation always present.*
6. **Session summary** — accurate reviewed count, again-rate, elapsed time, honest per-deck breakdown when mixed. *Acceptance: matches persisted grading history exactly.*
7. **Stats screen** — per-deck and overall: 30-day due-forecast bar chart, daily review-count history, retention rate; real Swift Charts views, honest empty/sparse handling, demo events excluded from aggregates. *Acceptance: renders correctly against real and sparse data with no fabricated values.*
8. **CSV export/import** — two-column (front, back) only; RFC4180-compliant parsing; preview before commit; every malformed row reported individually with a reason; duplicates (whitespace-trimmed, case-sensitive exact) skipped with a visible reason, not imported; post-import count reconciles exactly. *Acceptance: reimporting the same file produces zero new duplicates.*
9. **Daily local reminder** — one optional notification at a user-chosen time, generic non-numeric body text, toggle reflects true OS authorization status, clear re-enable path on denial. *Acceptance: notification body contains no digit; toggle never lies about permission state.*
10. **Demo-data toggle** — seeds two visibly-badged decks with realistic multi-day history; excluded from any deck cap and from aggregate stats; disabling it deletes every demo-flagged record, verifiable by count. *Acceptance: count query confirms zero demo rows remain after disabling.*
11. **Archive vs. delete** — modeled as distinct actions; archive reversible, delete explicit/confirmed/cascading. *Acceptance: delete removes deck + cards + history; archive does not.*
12. **Honest gaps** — cloud sync, shared/community decks, and a marketplace are never faked or stubbed; each is documented with a concrete "what building it for real would take" note.

**Should-have:**
- StoreKit 2 subscription/paywall (3-deck free cap, unlimited-deck/charts/CSV-import/reminder unlock, on-device entitlement, lapsed-locks-not-deletes) — real if built, but not required for this build to be considered complete; fallback is a fully-real free tier with no cap and no paywall UI at all.
- The four StoreKit-gated unlocks, contingent on StoreKit actually being built.

**Could-have:**
- Minor polish on the reveal-to-grade card-flip transition/animation (cosmetic only, doesn't gate correctness).

**Won't-build:** cloud sync, shared/community decks, a deck marketplace, tags, multiple card types, markdown/LaTeX rendering, widgets, Siri integration, any third-party SDK, accounts/login, intra-session Again requeuing (Anki-style relearning steps), a live due-count in the notification body, CSV export of the `note` field, and case-insensitive/fuzzy CSV duplicate matching.
